svg.text: Button, knob, dim on a breadboard
LP-MSPM0G3507, seen from above, USB unplugged. Add the wires in the numbered order; each number sits at both ends of its wire and in the list below. The schematic shows the same circuit in symbols.
J1 and J2 are the outer columns, J3 and J4 the inner ones; pin 1, 21, 40 and 20 are at the USB end.
Wire colours: red 3.3 V, orange 5 V, black ground; every other colour is one signal.

g.text: Breadboard: holes a to e, and f to j, in one column are joined; each long rail is joined end to end.
Column 1 is at this end; rails and holes count up toward the top.
Wires, in the order you add them
Ground rail (blue, hole 2) to J2 pin 20 (GND)
Place first: 330 ohm resistor, Red LED
Resistor, breadboard j3 to J4 pin 40 (PB4)
LED minus, breadboard j7 to Ground rail
Knob outer pin, breadboard j23 to 3V3 rail
Knob outer pin, breadboard j25 to Ground rail
Knob middle pin, breadboard j24 to J1 pin 2 (PA25)
330 ohm resistor: one leg in h3, other leg in h6
Red LED: long leg (+) in f6, short leg (flat side) in f7
10 k knob: one outer pin in g23, middle pin (wiper) in g24, other outer pin in g25
Button S2 (on the board): no wire, the program reads it on onboard (PB21).
Then plug in USB, run the build, and expect
Knob to the left: LED off. Knob to the right: LED full. In between it dims smoothly.
The same circuit as a schematic

svg.text: Fox Red Labs. Pins from the build's pin table, the one the program is built from; the 3D build on the page shows the same wiring step by step. Board picture: TI SLAU873E, figure 1-1.
